slides.title: RockawayX vaults under attack
slides.subtitle: riskdep on a mainnet fork, step by step · alerts on Telegram
slides.notes: Demo: scripts/demo-rock/demo-rock.sh (README next to it). Vaults and dependencies: docs/analysis/ROCK-VAULT.md. Run of scripts/demo-rock/demo-rock.sh on a fork at block 26,165,572, 2026-10-11; alerts from out/demo-rock/watch-*.jsonl.

slides.title: The question we answer
bullets: One deposit hides a chain of other contracts and people
If one link breaks: how much do I lose, and how fast?
Leaving costs something for sure; staying may cost more
riskdep finds the chain, watches it, and says stay or exit
slides.notes: The challenge brief (Belem Capital): identify a position's dependencies, estimate the impact when one fails, and help decide stay or exit despite execution costs.

slides.title: What a deposit really depends on
bullets: Your USDC goes into the vault, which lends it to borrowers who post strUSD
Those loans are safe only while the oracle prices strUSD correctly
The oracle reads a RedStone feed whose code can be replaced
Two signatures out of three are enough to do it, with no delay
slides.notes: Tori Ecosystem: 13.6M USDC, 69 % of it lent against strUSD (ROCK-VAULT.md, demo prediction). The 2-of-3 Safe owns RedStone's ProxyAdmin (scripts/fork/addresses.env, alt-redstone.sh).

slides.title: How the demo works
bullets: A fork is a private copy of Ethereum on the laptop
Scripts act as the real key holders: nothing real is touched
riskdep reads every new block, as it would on mainnet
Only real risks (warn and critical) reach Telegram
slides.notes: Fork at block 26,165,572 (anvil). Two watches: RockawayX Tori Ecosystem and Huma USDC Main. notify posts alerts at warn and above; start-up findings stay in the terminal.

slides.title: The words, in plain language
table: A pool of deposits lent out by a curator
The contract that tells the market what collateral is worth
A loan worth more than what backs it: someone loses
A wallet that needs several signatures (here 2 of 3)
A private copy of the blockchain, for rehearsing a crisis
Something changed / money is being lost now
slides.notes: Levels: docs/alert-runbook.md (critical: money is being lost now, or can be lost in the next block; warn: the risk changed, a decision may be needed).

slides.title: Act 1 · A forecast before the event
left: What if strUSD lost 32 % of its value?
Before anything happens on the fork
right: The book of 7 vaults loses 2.80M USD (2.8 %)
Act first on Tori: leaving pays if the risk is above 4.9 % over 30 days
slides.notes: Command: analyze --book examples/rockawayx-ethereum.json --shock token=strUSD:0.32. Same −32 % as act 2 causes, so the forecast comes before the event.

slides.title: Act 2 · The price feed is rewritten
bullets: RedStone's multisig swaps the code of the strUSD price feed
The new code says strUSD is worth 0.70 instead of 1.03
Loans become bigger than their collateral: 1.90M USDC of bad debt
Until it is written off, whoever stays in the vault carries it
slides.notes: alt-redstone.sh: oracle 1.0300 → 0.7001. UnrealisedBadDebt: 1,902,392 USDC, the vault's share 1,236,933 (9.09 % of the vault).

slides.title: Act 2 · What riskdep said
table: The code behind the price changed
The collateral lost a third of its value
1.90M USDC of loans no longer covered
In a rush to the exit, this depositor gets stuck
The oracle is 32 % below the market price
The loss, and the decision: EXIT
slides.notes: All six at block 26,165,574, the block after the upgrade. On Telegram: one summary (bad debt, exit queue, oracle move), the upgrade, and a second summary (divergence, impact).

slides.title: Act 2 · Stay or exit?
left: Loses 454,103 USDC: its share of the bad debt
Waits for the debt to be written off
right: 2,374,262 USDC can leave at full value
slides.notes: Depositor followed: the vault's largest, 0xddcd…cdd1, 4,994,682 USDC (36.7 %). Figures from the OracleImpact alert. Leaving first moves part of the loss onto those who stay: that is why speed matters.

slides.title: Is this a hack?
slides.notes: In the demo nothing is hacked: the fork is local. On-chain the three cases look identical; riskdep flags any upgrade, and the runbook says to check whether the new code is verified and announced, and to de-lever or exit until it is explained.

slides.title: Act 3 · Coins from nowhere
bullets: The bridge pool creates 15M PST, +7 % of the supply
Nothing backs these new coins
The oracle reads a rate, not the supply: it still says 1.138
riskdep flags the mint itself, in the same block
slides.notes: alt-pst-mint.sh 15000000: supply 213.9M → 228.9M PST. Admin.Mint is critical above 5 % of the supply in one transaction (watch.mint_share_critical); 10M (4.7 %) would stay silent.

slides.title: Reading a Telegram alert
bullets: Red (critical) rings the phone; orange (warn) arrives silently
First line: the level and the vault
Then what happened, the amounts, the block and a runbook link
Alerts of one block can arrive as one short summary
On the fork, the Etherscan link finds nothing: the transaction is local
slides.notes: riskdep notify: only alerts at warn and above, no heartbeat; standing findings once per 1800 blocks; criticals with sound.

slides.title: What to remember
bullets: A position depends on people and code you never see
riskdep names them, watches them and prices the damage
Each alert says what happened, what it costs and what to do
It cannot tell a hack from an upgrade: it flags both
Limits: a simulated crisis, prices read block by block
slides.notes: Run it: scripts/demo-rock/demo-rock.sh --manual (or PAUSE=10 for a slower pace; --no-telegram to rehearse).
